summary: Austria publishes the share of convictions for child sexual abuse and abuse material by Austrian citizens, and trafficking victims by nationality, but no citizenship of child victims in police statistics. Other origin figures appear only in parliamentary answers that count foreign suspects without Austrian totals.

nations.National (Statistik Austria, Interior Mi: Court statistics; police crime statistics; trafficking situation report; child-welfare statistics.
nations.Salzburg: Study of child-protection assessments for the Land Salzburg.

european_title: Not recorded by any Austrian source
european_note: Austrian official statistics record citizenship, never ethnic origin. 'Austrian' includes naturalised citizens and 'foreign' mixes EU and other Europeans with non-Europeans, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified.
proxy_note: Austria records citizenship, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual abuse of children (convictions)
harms.intro: Police recorded 363 victims of sexual abuse of children under 14 (section 207) in 2024, 277 girls and 86 boys, by age and sex only. Statistik Austria's court statistics give the citizenship of people convicted: Austrian citizens committed 76.9% of the convicted delicts of sexual abuse of children under 14 (sections 206-207) in 2024. Police counts of foreign suspects (112 for section 206 in 2024) appear only in parliamentary answers, with no Austrian total.

victims.text: Police statistics give child victims by age and sex only; no citizenship of victims is published.

perpetrators.scope: Austria, convicted delicts of sexual abuse of children under 14 (StGB sections 206-207), 2024
perpetrators.rate_reason: No rates by citizenship are published for these offences.
perpetrators.share_note: Share of convicted delicts committed by Austrian citizens, from the Statistik Austria report text; foreign = 100 minus 76.9, calculated here. Austrian citizens were 53.9% of all people convicted in 2024 and 71.9% within sexual offences. Citizenship, not ethnicity: Austrian statistics do not record ethnic origin. 'Austrian' includes naturalised citizens.

cross.text: No table links victim and perpetrator citizenship.

data.text: Parliamentary answer 570/AB counts foreign suspects of completed offences in 2024 (section 206: 112, of whom 8 asylum seekers; rape: 480) but gives no Austrian total, so no share can be calculated.

harms.label: Physical abuse and child-protection assessments
harms.intro: No national statistics give the citizenship of child victims of physical abuse. A study for the Land Salzburg gives the citizenship of minors in child-protection assessments for all concerns combined. Foreign suspects of torment or neglect of children or vulnerable people (section 92) are counted in a parliamentary answer (125 in 2024, including attempts) with no Austrian total.

harms.label: Murder
harms.intro: Police recorded 76 victims of reported murder offences in 2024 (36 male, 40 female), with no child victims by citizenship. Statistik Austria reports that Austrian citizens committed 49.5% of the convicted murder delicts in 2024 (all victims); a parliamentary answer counts 18 foreign suspects of completed murder, 2 of them asylum seekers.

harms.label: Trafficking in human beings
harms.intro: The Bundeskriminalamt identified 45 victims of trafficking (section 104a) in 2024: 28 for labour, 10 for sexual exploitation and 1 for begging among the adults, plus 6 minors (all girls). It lists the nationalities of all of them; the only Austrian victims were 2 girls (aged 12 and 15) among the minors. 36 suspects were investigated (25 male, 11 female), with no nationality given.

Minors: Moldova 2 and Bosnia-Herzegovina 2 (labour), Austria 2 (sexual exploitation and child trafficking). Shares calculated here. Citizenship, not ethnicity: Austrian statistics do not record ethnic origin. 'Austrian' includes naturalised citizens.

harms.label: Child sexual abuse material (convictions)
harms.intro: Statistik Austria reports that Austrian citizens committed 83.2% of the convicted delicts of child sexual abuse material (section 207a) in 2024. No victim data by origin are published; police counts of online grooming (section 208a) have no citizenship.

perpetrators.rate_reason: No rates by citizenship are published.
perpetrators.share_note: Share of convicted delicts committed by Austrian citizens, from the report text; foreign = 100 minus 83.2, calculated here. Citizenship, not ethnicity: Austrian statistics do not record ethnic origin. 'Austrian' includes naturalised citizens.

breakdown.why: Statistik Austria's court statistics give the share of convictions by citizenship: 76.9% of delicts of sexual abuse of children under 14 (sections 206-207) convicted in 2024 were by Austrian citizens (the report cites 163 delicts). Police statistics give foreign suspects only (112 for section 206 in 2024) through parliamentary answers, and victims by age and sex only. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

No national victim origin. A study commissioned by the Land Salzburg from its own child-welfare records gives child-protection assessments 2019-2023 by the child's citizenship (63.5% Austrian, 13.5% EU, 23% third-country), one state only, all concerns combined. Foreign suspects of torment or neglect of children (section 92) are counted only in a parliamentary answer. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Police statistics give 76 victims of reported murder offences in 2024 by sex and relationship, with no child victims by citizenship. Court statistics give Austrian citizens' share of convicted murder delicts (49.5% in 2024), all victims; a parliamentary answer counts 18 foreign suspects of completed murder. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

The Bundeskriminalamt 2024 situation report lists the nationalities of the 45 trafficking victims (none of the adults Austrian) and of the 6 minor victims (2 Austrian girls), and gives suspects by sex only; foreign suspects are counted in a parliamentary answer. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

Court statistics give 83.2% of child sexual abuse material delicts (section 207a) convicted in 2024 as committed by Austrian citizens (the report cites 499 delicts). No victim data by origin. Heritage points are 0 under the paired-data rule: no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm. Heritage points require that link as a published cross-table for the same child cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points and is awarded only for a published cross-table that records child victim heritage and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage. Coverage is 10, rates 7.5 and access 7.5. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points, and only when that pair is published. A published “White” category that merges Hispanic people or another group, so ethnic Europeans cannot be isolated, is scored as a proxy under the same cap. A country with no real ethnicity data is capped at 25%. Neglect is not part of the score.
score.why: Austria scores 10% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Heritage points are 0 because there is no published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data earns no heritage credit. Statistik Austria gives the share of convictions for child sexual abuse and abuse material by Austrian citizens, and the police trafficking report lists victims' nationalities, but citizenship is a proxy, police data on child victims have no origin, and other figures appear only in parliamentary answers.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 24 Nov 2026 (homicide 27.78, sexual abuse 22.22, sex trafficking 22.22, physical abuse 16.67, online exploitation 11.11); paired-data rule: heritage points only for a published child victim×offender cross-table

paired_child.basis: No published cross-table of child victim and offender heritage for the same cases. One-sided data scores 0 for heritage.
